newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain demands Cuba protect its Havana embassy.
newsitem.headline: Spain demands Cuba protect its Havana embassy.

text.p: Spain said on Wednesday it had called in the Cuban envoy to Madrid to demand special protection for the Spanish embassy in Havana after a diplomatic clash.

"I had the Cuban ambassadress in Madrid called in yesterday to be ... reminded of these responsibilities (of protecting the Spanish mission in Havana)," Foreign Minister Abel Matutes told a radio interviewer.
Elite Cuban troops were now guarding the Spanish embassy in Havana, Matutes said.
Several hundred Cubans congregated around the mission on Tuesday evening. Matutes said some were hoping to obtain Spanish visas.

Months of rising tension between Madrid and Havana boiled over on Tuesday when Cuba withdrew its earlier acceptance of a new Spanish ambassador and accused Spain's conservative government of "flagrant interference" in its affairs.

Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar has taken a tougher line against Cuba's Communist leader Fidel Castro than his Socialist predecessor Felipe Gonzalez. Spain is nudging its European Union partners into a tougher approach to press for democracy in Cuba.
